title: Rewiring the ribosome to translate proteins encoded in its own RNA.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. I confirmed: Europe PMC says not open access, not in PMC, no supplementary files, no text-mined accessions; NCBI elink from PubMed ID 42686901 returns zero links to GEO (gene expression repository), SRA (sequence read archive), BioProject, BioSample or Structure; Zenodo, Dryad and figshare searches on the DOI (digital object identifier) return zero records; PDBe (Protein Data Bank in Europe) returns zero entries for this citation title or for author Mankin; OpenAlex reports open-access status 'closed' with no repository full text; the Nature article page redirects to a login page (HTTP 303 to idp.nature.com).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the science comes from the PubMed abstract alone: that the authors appended a protein-coding sequence to 16S ribosomal RNA to make a chimeric messenger-ribosomal RNA (mrRNA), that this forms a ribosome called Ribo-M, that translation is blocked by small-subunit mutations and antibiotics, and that a tethered-subunit version called Ribo-TM was built. I could not read the Methods, the Data Availability statement, any figure, or any count of constructs tested.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. There is no downloadable dataset. The article is subscription-only (Nature page 303-redirects to a login service; OpenAlex open-access status 'closed'), it is absent from PubMed Central so Europe PMC can serve neither full text nor supplementary files, and searches of GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample, PDB/PDBe, Zenodo, Dryad and figshare on the DOI or PubMed ID all return nothing.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable, and moot: no table exists. Any label (e.g. reporter protein yield per construct) would have to be hand-transcribed from figures behind a paywall.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessable. The engineered mrRNA sequences are presumably in a supplementary table I cannot retrieve.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not verified, but this is a mechanistic study of a few named constructs (Ribo-M, Ribo-TM) plus mutational and antibiotic controls. Such papers report tens of measured variants, far under the ~1,500-row bar. Stated as an expectation, not a count I saw.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially true only because there is nothing to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare: no download and no methods text.

a8_label_provenance.note: Cannot trace. Likely reporter-protein fluorescence or luminescence and gel densitometry, but I could not read the Methods to confirm.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: no data from this paper is obtainable, so no model could be trained or evaluated on it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an engineered ribosomal RNA sequence to predict how much protein that self-translating ribosome makes.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on each engineered chimeric messenger-ribosomal RNA construct: its nucleotide sequence, where the protein-coding insert was placed in the 16S ribosomal RNA, and any linker or tether design. Number of examples: unknown, and almost certainly only tens.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be the amount of protein produced by that construct in cells or in a test tube, measured by a reporter assay such as fluorescence or luminescence, or by gel band intensity. I could not confirm which assay was used.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Synthetic biology groups building orthogonal protein-production systems would want a design rule for where to insert a coding sequence into ribosomal RNA without destroying ribosome assembly. In practice this paper supplies far too few designs to learn such a rule.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: predict protein output of a chimeric messenger-ribosomal RNA (a 16S ribosomal RNA with a protein-coding sequence grafted on) from its sequence and insertion-site design, as a design tool for orthogonal translation systems. Dead on arrival because neither the sequences nor the measurements are obtainable.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; there is no dataset to size. No timing was performed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask whether any machine-readable data exists: one Europe PMC open-access check plus NCBI elink to GEO/SRA/BioProject and a DOI search on Zenodo/Dryad/figshare. All returned nothing, which killed it in under five minutes.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright. The paper is paywalled and absent from PubMed Central, so no full text, Data Availability statement or supplementary file is retrievable, and no deposit exists in GEO, SRA, BioProject, PDB/PDBe, Zenodo, Dryad or figshare under this DOI or PubMed ID. Even if the supplement were opened, this is a mechanistic proof-of-concept about a handful of engineered ribosome constructs, so A5 (enough rows) would very likely fail too: the scientific claim is 'a ribosome can translate its own RNA', which is a yes/no demonstration, not a measured variant library.
